title: Tokenizer adapter + graceful chat-template degradation runbook for onboarding and model pins
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: During recent onboarding runs we observed several models producing tokenization divergence relative to Redwood's canonical tokenizer settings. These divergences cause chat template marker mismatches (role delimiters, system message framing) and inflate token counts versus the performance profile published during pinning, leading to inaccurate SLO budgeting and occasional runtime fallbacks.

Goal: Implement a lightweight tokenizer adapter and an onboarding runbook to detect, normalize, and gracefully degrade chat templates when tokenizer mismatches are detected. Ensure model pinning and performance profile publishing include gating checks that prevent publishing profiles with >10% token-count regression against expected baselines.

Scope: This ticket covers (1) design and implementation of the adapter and normalization rules, (2) integration into the onboarding pipeline and rollout gating for pins, (3) telemetry and alerting for template mismatches, and (4) an operator runbook for manual intervention during canary/publish failures. Not in scope: changing third-party model weights or upstream tokenizer releases.

Design notes: The adapter will live in the onboarding preflight stage (before deploying serving bundles). It will: 1) run a fast token-probing pass on the standard prompt corpus to compute per-message token deltas; 2) attempt deterministic normalization heuristics (strip/rewrite sparse whitespace, coalesce delimiter variants, map legacy role markers to canonical markers) and re-evaluate token deltas; 3) apply a template fallback when normalization cannot bring token delta under threshold — fallback preserves semantic roles but uses a simplified framing that is tokenizer-agnostic; 4) emit a structured compatibility report used by the pinning pipeline to block or allow profile publishing.

Telemetry and gating: The compatibility report includes: token delta histogram (expected vs observed), list of failed template markers, suggested normalization steps applied, and a compatibility-score. The profile publishing job will reject publishes where compatibility-score < 0.9 or median token delta > 10%. Rejections generate a Slack alert to #onboarding and create an internal ticket with pre-filled diagnostics.

Testing and verification: Add unit tests for normalization heuristics, integration tests exercising full onboarding flow with deliberately mis-tokenized model mocks, and a synthetic canary rollout exercising the fallback path. QA acceptance requires a simulated onboarding run demonstrating that the published profile token counts match observed serving token counts within 10% across 95% of probe prompts.

Runbook: Include step-by-step remediation: how to re-run adapter with expanded normalization, validate suggested PR changes to chat template, escalate to model ops if normalization masks semantic role loss, and rollback pin if publish continues to fail.

Acceptance criteria: 1) Adapter implemented and enabled in onboarding preflight; 2) Normalization heuristics documented and feature-flagged (default on for new model pins); 3) Compatibility report emitted and consumed by pin gating; 4) Profile publish blocked when regressions exceed thresholds; 5) Runbook documented and tested; 6) Observability: dashboards for token-delta and template-fallback rate added to Console.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter runs during onboarding preflight and emits compatibility report
Normalization heuristics reduce token delta <= 10% for >= 95% of probe prompts OR fallback template applied
Profile publish is blocked if compatibility-score < 0.9 or median token delta > 10%
Automated tests covering heuristics and canary fallback exist and pass in CI
Runbook published in Confluence and referenced in Slack alert payloads
Dashboard added for token-delta distribution and template-fallback rate
